newsitem.title: USA: GM reaches deal to end Indianapolis strike.
newsitem.headline: GM reaches deal to end Indianapolis strike.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Saturday it reached an agreement to end a costly United Auto Workers strike at an Indianapolis metal stamping plant that threatened to shut down nearly all of GM's North American truck production.

Patrick Morissey, a spokesman for GM's Metal Fabricating Division, confirmed that the deal with UAW Local 23 was reached at about 6:15 p.m. EST Saturday afternoon, about 14 hours after the automaker announced a tentative agreement with the union for a new national labor contract covering 215,000 UAW workers.

About 2,750 workers at the Indianapolis plant walked off the job because of a lack of progress in negotiations for a new local labor agreement. Company and union officials declined to comment on the grievances that were resolved.

The Indianapolis plant produces fenders, hoods, roofs and other steel stampings for nine of GM's 11 North American light assembly truck plants. As of Saturday, four of those plants were shut down by parts shortages, including facilities in Shreveport, Louisiana, Linden, New Jersey, Moraine, Ohio, Fort Wayne, Indiana.
A fifth plant, in Janesville, Wisconsin, was idled by a separate local strike that also started Tuesday.

Morrissey said Local 23 members in Indianapolis were scheduled to vote on the new local agreement on Sunday. If the pact is ratified, some production was expected to resume Sunday night, with the full workforce back on the job by Monday.
